To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the solution structure of the SECISE from the thermophillic bacterium Moorella thermoacetia and mapped the chemical shift perturbabions in the SelB protein upon binding to the SECISE.

the structure of the selenocys-teine insertion sequence (SECS) from the thermophillic organism Moorella thermo-acetica (SECISMT) determined using NMR spectroscopy, and the degree that chemical shifts of the backbone of the SECIS binding domain from M. thermoacet-ica SelB protein are affected by SECIS-MT binding.
the SECIS from Moorella thermoacetca has a pentaloop structure with a bulged-out nucleotide and that the third winged helix domain of SelB interacts with the SECIS RNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the three-dimensional structure of SECIS-MT and its interaction with SelB, the elongation factor responsible for the incorporation of selenocystein into proteins.

the structural and functional characterization of the SECIS RNA from the thermophillic organism Moorella thermoactica and its interaction with SelB, the elongation factor involved in the incorporation of selenocystein into a growing protein.

the three-dimensional structures of the SECIS-MT RNA hairpin and the SECIS-binding region of the M. thermoacetic SelB protein, which are important for the incorporation of the amino acid selenium into a growing protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NMR structure of the SECISE-MT hairpin and the chemical shift perturbation analysis of the SECIS binding domain of the SelB protein provide a detailed view of the molecular recognition between the two components.

the structure of the RNA and protein components of this system are known, and that the structure of a ternary complex of these components has been determined, and that the structural changes induced in the protein upon binding the RNA are known.
the structure of the M. thermoactica SECIS hairpin and its interactions with SelB are similar to the SECIS from Escherichia coli, but there are some differences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SECIS hairpin from M. thermoacetia has a unique structure and that the binding site for the SECIS hairpion is not limited to the previously known binding pocket in the third wing-helix domain of the selenocysterine-specific elongation factor.
SECIS-MT has a unique structure that differs from the previously reported structures for the Escherichia coli and human SECIS elements.

the structure of the M. thermoacetic SECIS RNA hairpin is highly similar to that of the SECIS RNA hairpins from other species, and that the interaction between the SECIS and SelB is similar to that of other SECIS-SelB complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SECIS-MT structure is different from previously published SECIS structures and that this structure may be representative of the structure of the majority of bacterial SECISs.

the SECIS hairpin is highly dynamic in the free state and that the binding of SelB to the SECIS is not a rigid-body interaction, but rather involves conformational changes on both the SECIS RNA and SelB protein.
the SECIS-MT RNA hairpin structure and its interaction with SelB are similar to those of their homologs from the human and E. coli SECIS.
